Full packet attached (blueleaf_incident_narrative_may20.pdf) and mirrored in the shared Drive link below.

High level summary:
- What happened: Brief KV-cache eviction cascade during a configuration rollout affected a subset of requests to your production tenant, causing elevated latencies and partial request failures between 09:12–10:07 PDT on 2027-05-20.
- Impact: ~6% request error rate and increased median latency from 65ms to 420ms for affected routes. No data loss; persistent storage and customer payloads were not compromised.
- Current status: Full rollback completed 2027-05-20 10:07 PDT; system metrics returned to baseline.

1) Please confirm receipt of the narrative and whether you'd like an executive readout (30m) this week.
2) Review the corrective roadmap (section 4 of the attached) and confirm whether the proposed SLO credit and remediation cadence are acceptable.

- A follow-up call; available windows attached in the calendar invite.

I appreciate BlueLeaf's direct feedback — our team will treat the action items as high priority.

Claire —

Joining briefly to give the technical timeline and immediate root-cause summary (see attached kvcache-metrics.csv for request-level traces):

Technical timeline (short):
- 09:00 PDT: Automated rollout A (service: prefix-cache-manager v2.3.1) begins; change increased default TTL eviction aggressiveness to reduce memory footprint under heavy tokenization workloads.
- 09:05 PDT: Gradual rollout hits 30% of instances in the West region. We did not detect abnormal errors during staged tests.
- 09:12 PDT: Coordinated eviction policy combined with a transient memory pressure event (node-level garbage collection spike triggered by a third-party telemetry collector update) caused accelerated KV eviction across ~30% of pool nodes.
- 09:14–09:45 PDT: Evicted keys caused a cascade of cache-miss traffic; backend cold-start behavior for those keys led to request queuing and increased tail latencies. BlueLeaf routes that rely on short-lived prefixes were particularly exposed.
- 10:00 PDT: Rollout halted and configuration reverted. 10:07 PDT: metrics returned to baseline.

Root causes (contributing):
- Primary: rollout of TTL policy change without an automated canary test covering the combined memory-pressure + eviction interaction.
- Secondary: telemetry collector update that coincided with the rollout increased GC activity on a subset of nodes; those nodes had been recently patched and had slightly higher memory fragmentation.
- Tertiary: lack of per-customer prioritization in the eviction strategy (global TTL change affected high-sensitivity tenants equally).

Immediate mitigations we've applied:
- Full rollback and rollout gating (already completed).
- Reverted telemetry collector version on affected nodes within 20 minutes.
- Emergency patch: per-tenant eviction weighting enabled to prioritize BlueLeaf and similar high-sensitivity accounts.

Near-term roadmap items (we will deliver these within the stated windows):
- Within 48 hours: Canary test that simulates combined GC and TTL stress (owner: Marcus Lin).
- Within 7 days: Conservative rollout policy change that includes per-tenant weights and automated abort on early latency signals (owner: Hannah Schmitt).
- Within 14 days: Post-release verification run and targeted BDD-style test for BlueLeaf workloads (owner: Marcus Lin).

I've attached the kvcache-metrics.csv excerpt and included the preliminary traces; happy to walk through the trace view on our call.
